Beginner Guide

Prep & Injection Guide

Basics of storage, supplies, syringe terminology and safer handling for products that are actually intended to be injected.

Before you begin: There is no universal preparation method for all peptides. The exact product instructions take priority over this general guide.

❄️ Peptide Storage

Heat, light, moisture, freezing and repeated temperature changes can affect some products. Store the exact medicine or research material according to its manufacturer, pharmacy or study instructions. Do not automatically freeze a product simply because it is lyophilized, and do not assume every reconstituted product has the same refrigerated shelf life.

🧴 Supplies

Depending on the prescribed product/device, supplies may include alcohol prep pads, an appropriate sterile syringe/needle, a sharps container and the medication. A diluent such as bacteriostatic water should be used only when the exact product instructions call for it.

📏 Syringe Basics

Common insulin-syringe capacities include 0.3 mL, 0.5 mL and 1 mL. Gauge describes needle diameter; a higher gauge number is generally thinner. Syringe “units” indicate a volume scale and do not by themselves tell you milligrams of a non-insulin medication.

💧 Reconstitution

Reconstitution means adding the specified diluent to a dry product. Only reconstitute a product when its legitimate instructions require it. Use the specified diluent and volume, clean vial stoppers as directed, avoid contaminating sterile components, and follow product-specific mixing and storage directions. If instructions are missing or the concentration is unclear, contact the dispensing pharmacy or prescriber before use.

💉 Subcutaneous Injection

Subcutaneous medicines are delivered into fatty tissue. Approved product instructions may identify appropriate sites such as the abdomen, thigh or upper arm and explain site rotation. Follow the exact medicine/device instructions and professional training you were given.

💪 Intramuscular Injection

Intramuscular injection requires correct site selection, needle length and technique. Not every peptide or injectable product is intended for IM use. If an IM medicine is prescribed and you have not been trained, ask a qualified healthcare professional to demonstrate the correct technique for that product.

♡ Important Reminders

  • Use sterile, single-use equipment.
  • Never share needles or syringes.
  • Never guess concentration or dose conversions.
  • Dispose of sharps safely.
  • Follow exact product storage instructions.
  • Do not use a product intended only for research as though it were an approved medicine.
Disclaimer: This guide is educational only and does not replace product labeling, pharmacist instruction or individualized medical advice.
